verdict.reasoning: Transcript: Doctor confirms, “you are feeling hot, and have had severe headaches,” and patient describes heart “beating, kinda fast” and later “I… noticed your heart beating?” / “maybe once a day,” consistent with intermittent palpitations.

Transcript: Patient: “I get this like, feeling of, short, like, short of breath, sometimes.” Doctor: “do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?” Patient: “Yeah… yes.” This is shortness of breath at rest (sitting).
Transcript: Patient: “I… kinda lose my appetite.” This supports decreased appetite.
Transcript: Doctor: “Is it in one hand? Or both hands?” Patient: “Both.” This supports tingling in both hands.
Transcript: Patient: “I do have like, some loss of libido at home.” This supports decreased libido.

Transcript: Patient: “But it started roughly when I changed jobs.” Symptoms described (headaches, SOB, palpitations, tingling, loss of libido) occur at different times: “Almost randomly… one time, one thing at a time,” supporting episodic occurrence since job change.

Headache features: Doctor: “where does the headache sit… front, or the back?” Patient: “mostly in the front… it just kind of stays there” (frontal, non-radiating). Location: “generally during, work times… I'm at work, I'm in a meeting, or on my laptop.” Commute: Doctor: “do you get these headaches on your commute in to work?” Patient: “Not really. I get it, mostly when I'm, at work.” Nausea: Patient: “I kind of feel a little bit nauseous maybe.”

Transcript: Palpitations: patient: “when I… come into the elevator… my heart is beating, kinda fast.” Frequency: “maybe once a day, uh, maybe more.” This supports almost daily palpitations noticed during activities like entering an elevator.

Transcript: SOB context: Patient: “I get this like, feeling of… short of breath, sometimes.” Doctor: “do you feel short of breath while you're sitting at your desk?” Patient: “Yeah… yes.” Doctor: “And, how about when you're exercising?” Patient: “No.” This matches SOB at rest (desk) and not with exercise.

Transcript: Tingling: Doctor: “Is it in one hand? Or both hands?” Patient: “Both.” Doctor: “And, do you get that in your legs as well?” Patient: “No.” Description: Patient: “Quick picking, yeah.” This supports bilateral hand paresthesias described as “quick picking” with no leg involvement.

Transcript: Decreased appetite: Patient: “I… kinda lose my appetite.” Weight loss: Doctor: “Have you lost weight?” Patient: “Yes.” Doctor: “Can you remember how much you've lost?” Patient: “Five pounds.” Doctor confirms it is “not intentional.” This supports mild unintentional weight loss of about 5 pounds with decreased appetite.

Transcript: Work pattern: Patient: “Like fifty-fifty. I go to meetings and then uh, sit in front of a computer.” Stress: Doctor: “If, uh, ten out of ten is, extremely stressful… Where would [you be]?” Patient: “Think it's, seven, or eight.” Doctor: “Yeah, it's like, a law firm, like, there's always pressure.” This matches stress 7–8/10 at a law firm with ~50% meetings and 50% computer.
Transcript: Patient: “well I have, hyperthyroidism.” This directly supports history of hyperthyroidism.

Transcript: Doctor: “do you take medications for that?” Patient: “Thyroxine.” Doctor: “And, are you remembering to take your medications?” Patient: “Yes.” This supports being on thyroxine with reported adherence.
Transcript: Patient: “I'm a lawyer.” Doctor: “do you work in London at the moment?” Patient: “Yes.” This matches being a lawyer working in London.

Transcript: Alcohol: Doctor: “How much do you drink?” Patient: “Like, once a week, couple of glasses, of wine.” Smoking: Doctor: “And, how about smoking?” Patient: “No.” Drugs: Doctor: “do you do anything else recreational, in terms of drugs?” Patient: “No.” This supports ~2 glasses of wine weekly and denial of smoking or recreational drug use.

Synthesizes supported elements: recurrent frontal headaches (“mostly in the front”) at work (“generally during, work times”), mild nausea (“a little bit nauseous maybe”), no radiation (“just kind of stays there”), onset since job change (“it started roughly when I changed jobs”).

Palpitations are documented (“my heart is beating, kinda fast… maybe once a day”) and SOB: at rest (“short of breath… while you're sitting at your desk?” “Yes.”) and not with exercise (“How about when you're exercising?” “No.”). This matches the summary.

Transcript: tingling in both hands (“Both.”) described previously, and first time noticed, occurring at different times among symptoms (“one time, one thing at a time”), supporting episodic bilateral hand paresthesias.
Same as hpi-006: decreased appetite plus unintentional 5‑pound weight loss (“Five pounds… It's not intentional, no.”).
Consolidates pmh-001 and med-001: hyperthyroidism (“I have, hyperthyroidism”) with thyroxine use and adherence (“Thyroxine… are you remembering to take your medications?” “Yes.”).

Transcript: Doctor: “I think the best course of action is, you come and see, one of our doctors, in the clinic.” and “I think you can book an appointment through the app, to come and see us clinic.” This supports arranging an in‑person clinic appointment via app.
Transcript: Doctor: “We can give you an examination, and what that means is, we check your heart and your breathing.” This is a cardiovascular and respiratory physical exam.
Transcript: Doctor: “And probably do some blood tests, for your thyroxine.” This is ordering thyroid blood tests.
Transcript: Doctor: “I think before we give you any medications, we should see you in person.” This indicates deferring medications until after examination (and implied investigations).
Transcript: Doctor: “I'll let them know what you've told me today, so you won't have to repeat exactly what you've said.” This is a handover of today’s history to clinic colleagues.
